public_rationale: The December 21, 2025 report puts OpenAI's compute margin across paid corporate and consumer products at 70% as of October 2025 [e1]. That measure deducts model-running costs and does not isolate subscription revenue and attributable subscription costs [e1]. It therefore neither establishes nor refutes substantial subscription losses at both companies during October–December 2025 [e1].
limitations: The packet lacks matching subscription revenue and cost records for either company for the full target quarter.
It does not show subscriber usage distributions or allocations of training, free-user costs, and other shared costs.
The reported compute margin does not establish overall subscription profitability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic and OpenAI lose a great deal of money on their subscriptions.

statement.excerpt: Even if these companies were profitable on inference (I do not believe they are), they are dramatically, horrendously unprofitable on subscriptions, and there isn’t a chance in Hell that the majority of those subscriptions convert into token-based API users.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

our_interpretation: The companies are Anthropic and OpenAI. The claim concerns each company's subscription business overall, not merely its heaviest users or an individual premium plan.
The ordinary reading is that subscription revenue falls substantially below attributable costs. No numerical loss threshold or accounting basis is supplied.

Use October–December 2025, the latest completed calendar quarter before the post that public reporting could describe. This period is an evaluator choice because the statement describes an ongoing state.
The hypothetical concession about inference profitability is not a condition on the subscription-loss assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable subscription revenue and attributable cost records show substantial subscription losses at both companies during the target quarter.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that at least one company's overall subscription business was profitable, broke even, or incurred only small losses during the target quarter.
